provenance: Self-authored synthetic English restaurant utterances created for this coursework prototype. These are not customer records, collected user feedback, or benchmark test examples. Each base utterance defines one augmentation family.

data_protocol.test_set_access: None. This script reads only training/data/intents.json; it does not read evaluation files.

selection_protocol.model: development macro F1 after rejection, then development accuracy, then raw development macro F1
selection_protocol.threshold: For each model maximise development macro F1, then accuracy, then choose the higher tied threshold for conservative rejection.
selection_protocol.model_tie_break: Declared candidate order after the recorded selection metrics tie.
selection_protocol.bounded_follow_up: After the original three-model comparison, evaluate LR C=[2,8,32] and SVC C=[0.5,2,8] at character weights [0.35,0.8], keeping the same fixed corpus and family split. All 15 candidate results are retained. No final test results are consulted.
selection_protocol.refit: No refit on development data. The saved model is the fitted training-only model.
selection_protocol.score_warning: Scores are uncalibrated model outputs, not accuracy estimates or probabilities that answers are factually correct.

limitations: Small self-authored synthetic English corpus; not representative of real restaurant customers.
The development set is used for model and threshold selection, so its scores are optimistic selection results, not final test estimates.
One bounded follow-up hyperparameter grid was chosen after reviewing the initial development scores. This repeated development use introduces further selection bias.
Polite-prefix augmentation does not add new semantic content; grouped splitting prevents its leakage across train and development.
Unknown topics beyond the fallback training examples can still be misclassified.
